name: Telegraf
what_it_is: Telegraf is a plugin-driven server agent for collecting, processing, aggregating, and writing metrics, logs, and other arbitrary data. It ships as a standalone static binary with no external dependencies and supports over 300 plugins.
components: Input plugins (300+): system stats (CPU, memory, disk, network), SNMP, gNMI, NetFlow, IPFIX, sFlow, MQTT, HTTP, Kafka, AMQP, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, OPC-UA, Modbus, Docker, Nvidia SMI, SQL, Exec, File/Tail
Output plugins: InfluxDB, Kafka, MQTT, HTTP, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, and many others
Processor plugins: transform, filter, and enrich metrics in-flight
Aggregator plugins: compute statistical summaries (min, max, mean, histogram) over time windows
Windows-specific plugins: Event Log, WMI, Performance Counters
measurement: Collects metrics at a configurable collection interval (default 10s)
Flushes to outputs at a configurable flush interval (default 10s)
Aggregators compute summaries (min/max/mean/percentiles) over sliding or tumbling windows
Supports tags (key-value metadata) and fields (numeric/string values) per measurement
Supports logs and traces in addition to metrics
configuration: Global agent settings: interval, flush_interval, metric_batch_size, metric_buffer_limit
Per-plugin filtering via tagpass, tagdrop, namepass, namedrop, fieldpass, fielddrop
Environment variable substitution supported in config files
Config directory support for splitting config across multiple .conf files
modes: Daemon mode: continuous collection and forwarding at configured intervals
Test mode (--test flag): run inputs once, print to stdout, no output plugins
Config test mode (--config-test flag): validate configuration without running
Once mode (--once flag): collect and flush exactly one cycle then exit
Plugin list mode (--input-list / --output-list): enumerate available plugins
constraints: No external runtime dependencies — statically compiled binary only
Windows-specific plugins (Event Log, WMI, Performance Counters) are not available on Linux/macOS
Plugin behavior and available options vary significantly; not all plugins support all field/tag filtering options
Metric buffer is bounded (metric_buffer_limit, default 10000); metrics are dropped if buffer fills before flush
Configuration is TOML only — no YAML or JSON config format supported natively
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml found in the repository root (404 on master branch)
No built-in fault injection or chaos engineering features
No native UI or dashboard — data must be visualized in a separate tool (e.g., Grafana, InfluxDB UI)
No built-in alerting — alerting must be handled downstream
